images.title: Ribbons and sixty thirds
images.purpose: Show that counting in 21s finds 63, a common multiple of 9 and 21, and that 7/9 = 49/63 is less than 17/21 = 51/63.
images.composition: One short multiples row at the top, then two long ribbons stacked below it with left edges aligned and wide space between them.
images.exact_structure: Top, centred: one row of three numbers 21, 42, 63 with 63 circled in reddish purple #CC79A7. Middle: one long flat ribbon cut into 9 equal pieces; the first 7 pieces filled teal #0072B2, the last 2 plain. Bottom: one ribbon of exactly the same length, left edges aligned, cut into 21 equal pieces; the first 17 pieces filled amber #E69F00, the last 4 plain. A thin dashed reddish purple vertical line drops from the end of the amber fill past the teal ribbon, showing the amber reaches further. Exactly 1 multiples row, 2 ribbons, 7 teal, 17 amber.

images.takeaway: Count in the bigger denominator to find a small common multiple, then compare the numerators.
images.description: Multiples of 21 reach 63, which 9 also goes into; a ribbon of 7 ninths and a same-length ribbon of 17 twenty firsts show 49/63 < 51/63, so the second ribbon is longer.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at 63 and say why 9 goes into it, then say which ribbon reaches further.

image_decisions.why: The multiples row and two equal ribbons show the small common multiple and the close comparison together.
